title: Show your product, pitch to shops, and plan 90 days
course_title: Product Packaging & Branding for Small Producers

say: Show your product, pitch to shops, and plan 90 days.
This is the video for Module 4 of Product Packaging and Branding.

Over this course you have made many pieces: a brand kit, label versions, a costing sheet, a test log and a compliance audit. Now pull them into one place. Create one folder in Google Drive for the project.

say: Zainab had notes and photos scattered across her phone and WhatsApp chats. In one afternoon, she created her folder and saved her brand kit and print-ready label.
She typed her paper costing sheet into Google Sheets. Packaging is about 145 naira, and her full cost is about 610 naira per unit.
She sells wholesale at about 870 naira, with a retail price of about 1,100.
Later, when a supermarket buyer asked for her product details, she sent one folder link in a minute.
Many buyers first meet your product as a photo on WhatsApp. Set a table beside a window with indirect daylight. Avoid harsh midday sun and yellow bulbs.

say: Then she asks what he would need before stocking it. He says customers ask for NAFDAC numbers, and the till needs a barcode. She writes it down, and follows up on WhatsApp that evening.

say: Before you leave goods on sale or return, agree in writing how many units, the price, when you will check stock, and when unsold or expired goods come back.

panel.heading: Three rules when dealing with shops

cards.d: Units left, price, when you check stock, and when unsold goods come back.
Keep a copy of every delivery note. A WhatsApp message is better than nothing.
Use NAFDAC, CAC and GS1 directly. Avoid agents who offer quick numbers.

say: Keep copies of every delivery note.

say: And use only official NAFDAC, CAC and GS1 Nigeria channels. A number someone arranges quickly outside the official process can be invalid and put your business at risk.

say: A good plan has a few actions, each with a date, a cost, and a way to know it is done. For example, Funke has a tested label for Ruby Zobo, but no registration yet.

panel.heading: Funke's 90-day plan
items: Days 1 to 30: CAC registration
Days 31 to 60: NAFDAC application, barcodes
Days 61 to 90: pitch cafes and a supermarket
Day 90: compare with your baseline

say: To remember. Keep your project in one clear folder. Photograph in daylight. Pitch with the shop's numbers, and follow up within a week. Agree terms in writing. And set targets you can count, like 70 bottles a week by day 90, not just sell more.

Pitch with the retailer's numbers
Agree sale-or-return terms in writing
Targets you can count, with a date

say: Now assemble your project folder, photograph your package and pitch to one real shop, then write your reflection and 90-day plan. You need at least 70% in the final quiz for your certificate.
